notes: 27 runs, gpt-4o-mini T=0, seed 20260916, 6-8 cases per corpus. Exact-substring scoring was a ruler defect (full-history 0.38 on support) — replaced by key-word matching and rescored offline. invalid_runs_discarded: e1-off-3 L (4 failed add jobs, machine slept)

notes: Gate = cloud/salience.py, lexical, no model call: rephrasings of an existing fact (weak-word-only difference), reported speech, passing states, session requests/questions, relation echoes on the other entity, assistant's own log. Not the pre-registered method (classifier on prod labels + Cohere embeddings): prod labels need a DB export Ali must run; the rule gate was measured first because it costs nothing at write time. Result: the gate never dropped a needed fact; it removes paraphrase and chatter (the whole of M's excess) but what is left at L is genuine facts no question asks about (neighbour's dog barks, octopus trivia), which a write-time gate should not remove. Two bench fixes on the way: adds are now sequential (parallel adds hid twins from the gate and exhausted the local pool), and failed jobs invalidate a run (E0/E0b on prod did not count them; their L numbers may carry silent failures). Decision: ship the gate ON by default? recall risk measured at zero on this corpus; junk -45% at the scale most accounts live at. Recommend: on by default in 2.45.0 with the drop reasons visible in the job result, and a demotion-by-recall-history experiment (E1b) for the L-scale remainder.

Reframed before running: the original E1b (demote facts by recall history) targeted the 18-23% of context that is facts; measurement showed the junk in the injected context is the raw conversation chunk fallback (5 per query). One chunk keeps every rescued answer (the 2/24 that extraction missed) at 45% fewer tokens; zero chunks loses 2 of 24. Shipped as `chunks` on /v1/search/all, default 1, 0..10. Replay, not re-extraction: same three E1 on-arm L memories on the local stack, same 600-token budget, same answer model. Fact-junk-by-recall-history stays parked until a corpus asks questions mid-history.

notes: The extractor was NOT the culprit: on the exact turns in isolation it returns 'has loyalty number LR-11560', 'uses Visa ending 4471', 'requested pickup at the central station office'. The contradiction pass was: it archived 'has loyalty number LR-11560' for 'has a loyalty number with the Assistant', 'always needs one child seat' for 'does not need a child seat for the business trip', 'uses Visa ending 4471' for 'used Mastercard ending 9083 for a hotel' (read from the local archive). Fix: cloud/store/_supersede.py — four deterministic guards (a vaguer restatement may not drop a value; one occasion does not override a standing fact; a one-off does not override the default; someone else's fact never archives the person's) plus the same rules in the prompt. The gate's request rule was the fourth loss ('requested pickup at the central station office'); narrowed to advice/idea/list requests. Junk at L rose 0.06 because facts that used to be (wrongly) archived now stay. Shipped as 2.45.3.
